question: Which institute developed the siphon-powered thermal desalination system that converts seawater into clean drinking water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Science (IISc).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The siphon-powered thermal desalination system was developed by researchers at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The system uses a siphon made of fabric wick and grooved metal surface to convert seawater into clean drinking water.**
 
• **This innovation significantly boosts desalination efficiency, producing over six liters of potable water per square meter per hour under sunlight.**
 
• **The system can operate entirely on solar power or waste heat, making it ideal for off-grid and disaster-hit regions.**
 
• **The system can handle salt concentrations up to 20%, making it effective for brine treatment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Indian Institute of Science (IISc)__

 __
 
• IISc, based in Bengaluru, is one of India's premier institutions for advanced research and education in science and technology.
 
 
 
• Department of Science and Technology (DST)__
 __
 
• The system was published in the journal *Desalination* and supported by DST, which promotes scientific and technological research in India.
 
 
 
• Desalination Process__
 __
 
• The new system enhances the desalination process by using a unique siphonage technique, significantly improving efficiency and reducing costs.
 
 
 
• Brine Treatment__
 
 
• In addition to desalination, the system's ability to handle high salt concentrations makes it a valuable tool for brine treatment in coastal areas.
